source.title: Disentangled Sparse Representations for Concept-Separated Diffusion Unlearning
source.authors: Hyeonjin Kim; Hangyeol Jung; Heechang Yun; Sung-Ju Yun; Dong-Jun Han

record.tranche_reason: The study measures concept-level overlap and separation in sparse autoencoder representations for text-to-image diffusion models, a new setting relative to the claim. It does not test the claim’s specific over-capacity, sparsity-dependent superposition account.
record.gate_note: The paper reports measurements of concept clustering, selected-feature overlap, and sparse probing in diffusion-model SAEs. These bear on sparse feature organization but do not measure whether more features than dimensions are represented as overlapping directions, or whether sparsity and importance determine that geometry. General unlearning-performance results are not recorded as rows because they do not directly measure the claim’s representational geometry.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs as a tool for diffusion-model concept unlearning and reports its own method's (SAEParate) performance against a vanilla SAE baseline. Its cluster-rate, centroid-margin, selected-feature overlap and k-sparse probing results measure concept separation in a supervised, contrastively trained SAE latent space. None measures whether a model stores more sparse features than dimensions as overlapping directions, why neurons are polysemantic, or whether unsupervised SAE features are canonical units. The separation is induced on purpose by the contrastive objective. The record's 'tests/T3' is therefore downgraded to T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAEParate gives concept-discriminative sparse representations with reduced feature overlap and state-of-the-art unlearning on UnlearnCanvas and I2P. They note it requires supervision and inherits SAE feature splitting and absorption.
record.recipe_differences: This is a supervised, concept-aware SAE training and inference-time unlearning method for text-to-image diffusion models, using spatial aggregation, contrastive learning, and a nonlinear encoder; it does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to contrastive-loss weight, encoder nonlinearity, SAE insertion layer, and inference-time suppression hyperparameters; these affect its own unlearning and cluster results, not a test of the claim’s superposition geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Vanilla TopK SAEs on SD v1.5 activations share selected latents across concepts (object overlap count mean 0.71, max 2). A supervised contrastive SAE with a nonlinear encoder removes this overlap, at a reconstruction cost (FVU 0.172 to 0.217).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reconstruction-only SAEs on diffusion activations do not yield concept-separated features; adding supervised concept separation trades reconstruction fidelity for concept-specific feature groups.

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
record.problems: The experiments are on text-to-image diffusion models, not toy networks or LLMs, and do not vary feature sparsity or compare feature count with representation dimension. The reported cluster and overlap analyses measure concept separation rather than the claim’s capacity-limited superposition geometry. Some plotted results are not numerically described in the text.
record.rows_left_out: General UA, retention, image-quality, efficiency, robustness, and sequential-unlearning results were left out because they do not directly measure the claim’s representational geometry. Figure-only UMAP comparisons without stated quantitative values were also omitted, except where the text explicitly describes feature-overlap findings.

untested.parts: No toy models; no feature-to-dimension comparison, sparsity transition or geometry.
No neuron polysemanticity or capacity-allocation analysis.
No analysis of the causes of polysemanticity.
No LLMs. SAEs are used on diffusion U-Net activations only as an unlearning tool, not as evidence of superposition.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity. The paper only mentions feature splitting and absorption as inherited limitations.

missing.what: Reconstruction FVU trade-off: vanilla SAE 0.172 vs SAEParate 0.217.
missing.versions: none (bears only on the fits_no_version finding)

record.verdict_notes: This is an applied unlearning-method paper. All rows compare the authors' supervised SAE against a vanilla SAE baseline, and the separation is engineered by a training objective. It is not evidence for or against any superposition version. The record's reader correctly left all rows at 'none' but mislabelled the relation and tranche.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-count-to-dimension comparison, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular superposition geometry.
Does not test neuron polysemanticity or whether limited capacity causes important features to receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Does not test polysemantic neurons or determine whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
The experiments concern text-to-image diffusion models, not LLMs; no neuron-level feature spreading or LLM SAE recovery is measured.
The paper does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units. It notes that feature splitting and absorption may limit concept capture.
Does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.check: Figure 4 values are readable: vanilla overlap max 2, mean 0.71; SAEParate max 0, mean 0.00. Max cosine similarity: vanilla mean 0.45, SAEParate mean 0.10. This is still a method comparison.
